_: Little Big Questions: How is a volcano born? Free narration (Kokoro, sound.yml) and the free score. Words exactly as the vo lines; facts in docs/research/KIDS_FACTS_2026-10.md.

vo.text: Far below us, it is so hot that rock can melt.
Melted rock is called magma. It is lighter than the rock around it, so it rises.
It finds a crack. Gas bubbles push, like a shaken fizzy drink. The ground rumbles.
Whoosh! It bursts out of the top. Now we call it lava.
The lava cools, and turns into brand new rock.
Each eruption adds a layer, and the mountain grows.
When the volcano rests, plants find a home on the new rock, and slowly it turns to rich soil.
The islands of Hawaii were built this way, one eruption at a time.
Our planet is always making new land, and the ground under your feet is slowly moving.
